editorial:
Imagine waking up one day and deciding to completely change who you are just to see what happens. That is basically what you get with this look at Bob Dylan's early years. You follow him from being a quiet folk singer in coffee shops to becoming a massive rock star that everyone in the world was talking about. It feels like a road trip through the sixties, showing how one man managed to stay ahead of everyone else while the crowd tried to tell him who to be. The vibe is curious and a bit rebellious, making you feel like you are spying on a legend while he figures things out in real time.

What really works here is how the movie shows the tension between Dylan and his fans who hated that he plugged in an electric guitar. The pacing stays steady, and the old footage is great, though some parts might feel a bit slow if you are not into music history. If you love music or just like seeing someone break the rules, you need to see this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick watch, but if you really love the sound and look, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is the way to go for the best quality.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing the peak of the chaos during Dylan's 1966 tour. You see him facing angry crowds who think he betrayed folk music. It ends with him essentially walking away from the spotlight for a while. The big takeaway is that he refused to be a puppet for any one group of people. He chose his own art over fame, leaving you to realize that his true goal was always total freedom.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music history or stories about rebels.
